exam_guide_revision: Reviewed anti-boring v4, 2026-09-26. Full learning and question editorial audit completed; weak/generic prompts and distractors were rewritten while preserving compatibility.

learning_design.unlock_rule: All learning reveals are required. Each node moves quickly through a concrete problem, the obvious failure/waste, the maintained state or invariant that fixes it, the pattern name, a different real-world transfer, and one quick check.
learning_design.mastery_note: The goal is not to enjoy studying algorithms. The goal is to recognize the structure fast enough that an unfamiliar problem starts to look like a problem you have already solved.

nodes.title: Sorting is worth paying for when it turns a global mess into local neighbors

reveal.text: Records may be reordered and you need to group equal customer IDs. You are learning to use sorting as preprocessing when order exposes adjacency, grouping, or a simple scan.

reveal.text: Repeatedly searching the whole unsorted collection for each customer's matching records can duplicate work.

reveal.text: Sort once by customer ID. Equal IDs become adjacent; one scan can identify group boundaries.

spans.text: ordered adjacency created by preprocessing

reveal.text: Sort → scan. Trigger: reordering is allowed and order makes matching/grouping/merging local

reveal.text: Interval merging, duplicate grouping, sweep-line scans, and ordered comparisons often start by buying useful adjacency with a sort.
